answer: Bind each identity to a single hardware enclave: the agent's key is born inside the chip's ferrous root of trust and can never leave it, so no mirror copy can spawn a twin. When an identity sets out on a voyage — joining a market, casting a vote, claiming a reward — it presents a fresh attestation proving the key still lives in real silicon. A sybil farmer needs one physical device per fake, and each chip costs real money and shelf space, while one honest agent rides on the phone or laptop they already own. Cloning is stopped by physics, not by fees.
